description: Iraq invades Kuwait, triggering the Gulf War and fears over regional oil supply; Brent spikes sharply in the following weeks.
Collapse of the Thai baht triggers a wider Asian financial crisis, sharply reducing regional oil demand through 1998.
Combined effect of the Asian crisis and OPEC oversupply drives Brent to roughly $10/barrel, among the lowest real prices of the dataset period.
Terrorist attacks on the US trigger a global demand shock and market uncertainty, contributing to a short-term price dip.
Start of the Iraq War raises concerns over Middle East supply disruption and adds a geopolitical risk premium to prices.
Brent reaches an all-time high near $147/barrel amid strong demand and speculative activity, just before the Global Financial Crisis hits.

event_name: Lehman Brothers Collapse / Global Financial Crisis
description: The Lehman Brothers bankruptcy triggers the Global Financial Crisis; oil demand collapses and Brent falls from ~$100+ to under $40 within months.
Political uprisings across the Arab world and civil conflict in Libya disrupt regional oil production, pushing prices higher.
Brent peaks near $115/barrel before a sustained decline driven by rising US shale output and weakening global demand.
OPEC's Vienna meeting maintains output at 30 million bpd despite oversupply, accelerating the 2014-2016 price collapse; Brent falls over $6 in a single day.
OPEC and non-OPEC producers (including Russia) agree to their first coordinated production cut in years, helping stabilize prices after the 2014-2016 collapse.

event_name: US Withdrawal from Iran Nuclear Deal (JCPOA)
description: The US announces withdrawal from the JCPOA and plans to reimpose sanctions on Iranian oil exports, raising supply concerns.

event_name: US Reimposes Sanctions on Iranian Oil Exports
description: Formal reimposition of US sanctions targeting Iran's oil sector tightens expected global supply.
Russia's refusal to deepen OPEC+ cuts leads Saudi Arabia to slash official selling prices and raise output, causing Brent's steepest single-day drop in decades.
Brokered partly by the US, OPEC+ agrees to cut ~9.7 million bpd amid collapsing COVID-19 demand, the largest coordinated cut in history.
Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine triggers Western sanctions on Russian energy exports and major supply-security concerns, pushing Brent above $100/barrel.
